name: E1: strict reliability evaluation of the per-history waiting rules on B3 with frozen rules and disjoint receiver roles
reason: Revision plan E1 (P0). The earlier waiting studies calibrated thresholds on one half of the posterior samples, used the same half as estimator references (leave-one-out by index), scored the other half, and reported the calibration target 0.94 after the target 0.90 had missed the per-history requirement in about half of the splits. The author posterior file also repeats 52 parameter vectors, so a plant could have an identical twin among its references. This study fixes the rule family, the calibration criterion, the infeasibility fallback and the reporting before any result is computed, separates reference, calibration and test receivers, and reports test success rates with one-sided confidence bounds.
unchanged: Simulation tables simulation/results/b3/readiness_tables.npz (1000 posterior samples; 25 ng/ml; 3- and 30-min previous commands ending at time 0; 5-min probe; decision grid 0-120 min in 2-min steps); task: success if the rise within W = 20 min of the probe is >= kappa = 0.5 x the same sample's naive rise; completion = wait + 20 min on success, D = 140 min on failure; estimators of b3_waiting (current; smoothed with scales 2, 4, 8, 16 min; B3 belief, key 'history'; likelihood s.d. max(noise, 0.001), smoothed s.d. as in b3_waiting.smoothed_sd); running-maximum threshold crossing as in b3_waiting_frontier.crossing_index; if the estimate never reaches the threshold the probe is sent at 120 min; fine threshold grid 0.50, 0.51, ..., 0.99; one parameter per previous command for every rule.
sampling_unit: A receiver is one distinct B3 posterior parameter vector (948 distinct vectors among the 1000 rows; the first occurrence of each is used) together with one independent draw of Gaussian observation noise on its history-only reporter. Success probabilities therefore refer to receivers drawn from the distinct posterior vectors with independent reporter noise: uncertainty about the population-mean parameters of one model structure, not cell-to-cell heterogeneity and not measured cells.
roles: For split r (0-19) the 948 distinct vectors are permuted with seed 20261009 + r and cut into reference R, calibration C and test T receivers (316 each, disjoint). Estimator references (kernel pairs and B3-belief particles) are the R receivers' noise-free trajectories and model outcomes; rule parameters are chosen on C with R as references; T is scored once with R as references and the chosen parameters. No receiver is in its own reference set and no twin crosses roles. Observation noise for split r: b3_waiting.noisy_observations with seed 20261109 + 100000 r. Split 0 is the primary split; the 20 splits report stability of one finite posterior set, not 20 biological experiments.

arms.certified: Primary. For each rule and history h a one-sided binomial test of H0: S_h(theta) <= 0.9 against S_h(theta) > 0.9 on the 316 calibration receivers, p = P(Bin(316, 0.9) >= k), in a fixed sequence from the most conservative to the most aggressive parameter, stopping at the first p > alpha_h (fixed-sequence testing). alpha_h = 0.025 per history, so the two per-history statements hold jointly at 0.95 (Bonferroni). Orders: thresholds 0.99, 0.98, ..., 0.50 for current and B3 belief; for smoothed one chain per scale (2, 4, 8, 16 min), each tested at alpha_h / 4; fixed waits 120, 118, ..., 0 min. Among all admitted parameters of the rule the smallest calibration mean completion is chosen (ties: smaller scale, then smaller threshold, then smaller wait). If nothing is admitted for a history, that history's probe is sent at 120 min and the rule is marked not certified for it; the receivers are scored like all others. With 316 calibration receivers the test needs >= 295 successes (93.4%) at 0.025 and >= 298 (94.3%) at 0.00625.
arms.plugin_090: Plug-in target 0.90: smallest calibration mean completion among parameters with calibration success >= 0.90 (b3_waiting_frontier.choose); if none reaches it, the parameter with the highest calibration success.
arms.plugin_094: As plugin_090 with target 0.94, the target reported in the earlier Table II; flagged as chosen after the earlier evaluation results were known.

test_metrics: On T per arm, noise, rule (fixed, current, smoothed, B3 belief) and history, and for the oracle: n, successes, success rate, one-sided 95% and 97.5% Clopper-Pearson lower bounds, mean failure-penalized completion, mean completion among successes, mean wait, failures (probe sent but task failed), certified flag; paired per-receiver differences of each adaptive rule minus the same arm's fixed waits in completion and success, per history and averaged over the two histories, with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals over test receivers (2000 resamples, seed 20261012). 'Meets per history' = test success >= 0.9 for both histories; 'joint bound' = both 97.5% lower bounds >= 0.9.
summary: Over the 20 splits per arm, noise and rule: splits meeting 0.9 per history on test; splits with the joint bound >= 0.9; splits certified for both histories; median, minimum and maximum of test success per history, completion and paired differences; splits in which the adaptive rule is faster than the fixed waits.

statements.E1-S1: Certified arm, split 0, noise 0.005: test success per history with its one-sided 95% lower bound for fixed, current, smoothed and B3 belief, and the number of splits (of 20) meeting 0.9 per history.
statements.E1-S2: Same setting: paired completion difference of each adaptive rule minus the certified fixed waits with its 95% interval (split 0), its median over the 20 splits and the number of splits in which it is negative.
statements.E1-S3: Plug-in 0.90 arm, noise 0.005: number of splits meeting 0.9 per history on test for each rule.
statements.E1-S4: Noise 0.005: median over splits of the certified minus plug-in-0.94 completion for each rule (the cost of the derived margin).

checks: Freeze hash; roles disjoint, distinct and twin-free; leakage: inverting every test outcome leaves every chosen parameter unchanged; a calibration table with no successes makes every certified choice a fallback scored at 120 min; splits 0 and 7 recomputed from scratch equal the saved results within 1e-12; the 20-split summary and E1-S1 to E1-S4 re-derived with independent code from the saved per-split numbers.
known_before_freezing: Earlier Table II (b3_waiting_frontier, target 0.94, noise 0.005, 500/500 halves, leave-one-out references): medians over 20 splits of the mean completion: fixed 122.06, current 122.21, smoothed 114.49, B3 belief 114.89, oracle 105.00 min; every rule met 0.9 per history in 20 of 20 splits; with target 0.90 in 7-11 of 20 and with 0.92 in 16-19 of 20. The twin audit (results/audit/waiting_design_audit.json) found 19-33 evaluation plants per split with a twin among the references and changed the median B3-belief-minus-fixed completion from -7.19 to -7.11 min when they are excluded; no calibration target was missed in the earlier study. The derived certification margins above were computed before freezing. No E1 quantity has been computed.
interpretation_limits: All 948 vectors were used while the rule family, grids and earlier targets were developed, so E1 is a frozen re-evaluation of seen parameter vectors: it covers the sampling variation of the role split and the observation noise, not unseen receivers, structural model error or cell heterogeneity. Calibration uses every calibration receiver's complete outcome curve (ideal information); limited probes are studied in E2. The certified statement is conditional on the references and on receivers being exchangeable draws from the distinct posterior vectors.
reporting: All arms, rules, noises, splits and fallbacks reported whatever their direction. No threshold, target or arm is changed after the run; a failed run is recorded and a corrected protocol frozen before the single rerun.
